question: A 59-year-old woman is admitted to the intensive care unit after surgery following a motor vehicle collision. She has received a total of four units of packed red blood cells. Physical examination shows dry mucous membranes and flat neck veins. Serum studies show a creatinine of 2.1 mg/dL and urine microscopy shows granular, muddy-brown casts. A renal biopsy specimen is obtained and examined under light microscopy. Which of the following reversible cellular changes is most likely to be present?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hypovolemia due to blood loss -> Decreased renal perfusion -> Acute tubular necrosis -> Swelling of the mitochondria -> 80% CHAIN: Ischemic injury to the kidneys -> Disruption of cellular organelles -> Swelling of the mitochondria -> 75% CHAIN: Acute kidney injury from hypoperfusion -> Cellular injury -> Swelling of the mitochondria -> 80%
analysis: The clinical presentation of dry mucous membranes, flat neck veins, elevated creatinine, and muddy-brown casts in urine suggests acute kidney injury (AKI) with acute tubular necrosis (ATN) as a possible cause. In ATN, there is cellular injury to the renal tubular epithelial cells. Among the given options, swelling of the mitochondria is a reversible cellular change that can occur in response to cellular stress or injury.
